links.note: A pencil looks bent at the water surface because light bends on leaving water - refraction (229). The amount of bending would be 231, but this item only asks why it bends at all.
A torch or headlight bulb sits at the focus of the concave reflector so the reflected rays leave parallel - concave-mirror ray behaviour by object position (238), not the naming of parts (225).
The pencil bends differently in kerosene or turpentine because those media have a different refractive index (231), which is exactly what separates this item from the plain refraction item 86649.
Defines a reflector as a surface that reflects light (222).
Only the concave mirror can give a real image of a real object - the distractors are a plane mirror, convex mirror and concave lens, all of which give virtual images (238).
A ray through the focus is reflected parallel to the principal axis - one of the ray rules used to construct concave-mirror images (238).

Relates dioptre power to focal length and sign of the lens - power of a lens (237). KEY DEFECT: the marked answer says a CONCAVE lens has +4 D at f = 0.25 m; a concave lens has negative power, so the true statement is option (a), the convex lens.
